name: PPT Master
cost: Free and open source (MIT). You pay for the AI model you use.
works_with: Any agent that can read and write files and run commands, such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot and Cline
short: Turns a PDF, Word file or pasted text into a PowerPoint deck you can keep editing, with real shapes, charts and tables.
what: PPT Master is a workflow (a skill) that runs inside your coding agent. You point it at a document or paste some text, and it plans the slides, designs them and exports a .pptx made of native PowerPoint objects. It can also fill an existing deck with new content, build templates from your references, and add transitions, animations and narration.
who: Anyone who makes decks from reports or notes and wants slides they can still edit in PowerPoint. The author says you only need to install Python and an AI tool, with no coding. The README is frank that cheaper models leave more polishing to you, so expect to tidy the result.
needs: An agent-capable AI tool. The author develops and tests on Claude Code
Git, for the recommended clone install (or download the ZIP instead)
Pandoc, only for older formats like .doc, .odt, .rtf or .tex
Optional: an image provider API key, or free Pexels or Pixabay keys for better stock photos

steps.title: Get the project
steps.text: Cloning lets you update later. A ZIP download from GitHub works too.

steps.title: Or install it as a skill
steps.text: This fetches only the skill files. You still run `pip install -r requirements.txt` from the installed location.

steps.title: Open the folder in your agent
steps.text: In an editor, use File, Open Folder. In a terminal agent, `cd ppt-master` and start it there. Put your source files in the `projects/` folder.

steps.title: Optional: add image keys
steps.text: Keys for image generation or Pexels and Pixabay go in a `.env` file. In a clone, start from the example file.

steps.title: Update later
steps.text: For clone installs. It pulls the latest version and syncs the Python dependencies.

try.label: From the README
try.where: Your agent's chat, inside the ppt-master folder
try.text:
Please create a PPT from projects/q3-report/sources/report.pdf

It confirms a design spec first. To skip that, ask for a quick 5-page deck and say there's no need to confirm. The deck lands in `exports/`.

watch: The pipeline runs on your machine, but your source material goes to whichever AI model you use.
Your agent needs to read and write files and run commands for this to work.
Image keys live in a plain `.env` file. Keep it out of anything you share or commit.
The README links to paid model resellers that sponsor the project. You don't need them if you already have model access.
Windows needs extra setup steps. The project has a separate Windows guide.
